findings.title: Correct the grant shortcut assertion
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies indexes 4–5, so it must be read with substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). The comparison is also inverted: equality currently rejects the token. Consequently, an ID such as onrtrt:<uuid> passes an assertion expecting the authorization-code shortcut ac, allowing incorrect or missing grant metadata to go unnoticed. Check the prefix length and reject when the correctly extracted shortcut does not equal the expected value.

findings.title: Specify the required two-character grant shortcut
findings.body: This contract recommends a three-character shortcut, but the default decoder requires a six-character context prefix containing exactly two characters per field. A custom factory returning a documented three-character shortcut is accepted during registration and produces IDs such as onrtabc:<id>, which the decoder then rejects for having a seven-character prefix. Document the exact two-character requirement and validate it when registering factories.

findings.title: Ensure the invalid-grant test exercises the intended exception
findings.body: The test fixture never initializes the factory's sessionFactory. Because ac is absent from its shortcut map, decoding enters getGrantTypeByShortcut's provider-discovery fallback and throws NullPointerException when accessing sessionFactory. Catching any RuntimeException makes the test pass without reaching the intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Supply a mocked session factory with no matching provider and assert the specific exception.

findings.title: Validate rawTokenId instead of checking grantType twice
findings.body: The rawTokenId null check mistakenly checks grantType again. A context with a valid grant type and null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId serializes its identifier as the literal suffix :null instead of rejecting the missing identifier. Pass rawTokenId to this requireNonNull call to enforce the constructor's intended invariant.
